Musa is a messenger whom Allah the Exalted sent to Pharaoh and his people, and supported with two miracles: one of them is the staff that swallowed the serpents; the other was his hand, which he would put into his bosom and it would come out white without any blemish. Musa called to the oneness of Allah, so Pharaoh fought him and gathered the sorcerers against him to plot against him, but he defeated them by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Then Allah commanded him to leave Egypt with those who followed him, and Pharaoh pursued him with a great army; and when his followers thought they would be overtaken, Allah commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, so that it would be his salvation and the destruction of Pharaoh, whom Allah made a lesson for others.

When Moses returned and saw what his people had come to, he reproached Aaron severely.

Nuh was pious and truthful; Allah sent him to guide his people and warn them of the punishment of the Hereafter, but they disobeyed him and called him a liar. Despite this, he continued to call them to the upright religion, and a few people followed him, while the disbelievers persisted in their transgression. So Allah withheld the rain from them, and Nuh called them to believe so that Allah would lift the punishment from them; they believed and Allah lifted the punishment, but they returned to their disbelief. He kept calling them for nine hundred and fifty years; then Allah commanded him to build the ark and to take with him a pair of every kind; then the flood came and drowned them all.
